items.name: login-form-react
items.title: Login Form (React)
items.description: Credential card composing the @moderno-ui/react Card, Field, PinInput, Checkbox, Button and Alert primitives, in any of its five modes: sign-in (email, password, remember-me, recovery link), sign-up (full name, email, a new password and consent), forgot-password (the address alone, and the same card confirming once the link is sent), reset-password (a new password and its confirmation, the rules ticking off as they are met, and the emailed token in a hidden input) or verify (one cell per digit of a one-time code, the address riding along in a hidden input, and a second submit that asks for a new code once the countdown is up). Responds to its container (@container) rather than the viewport, renders its default, disabled, loading and error states from props, and takes the heading rank its title carries (titleLevel) so a screen can mount it as the whole route.

items.description: A header bar with actions for a page, a section or a card, composing the @moderno-ui/solid Alert, Badge, Button, Card and Skeleton primitives: a page header carries a breadcrumb trail, a display heading and a status line, a section header sits on a rule and a card header tops a card that holds the body passed to it, each with a secondary and a primary action and its own empty, loading and error renders; responds to its container (@container) across all three contract steps — the full trail and the actions beside the heading at @sm, a larger heading at @md, the largest heading and a larger description at @lg.

items.name: stacked-list-react

items.name: auth-react
items.title: Auth flow (React)
items.description: Example assembly for the auth flow: sign-in → sign-up → forgot-password → reset-password → verify. It owns the navigation state the five screens refuse to hold — which step is on the route, the address carried between them, the reset token, the seconds left on the verify resend and the two confirmations a card paints once a recovery link or a fresh code has gone out — and it moves between them the way a client router does: the screens draw plain hrefs (hrefFor), the assembly intercepts the clicks it owns and leaves modified clicks and every other link to the browser, and each forward step is a form submission read with its submitter. Rewrite it against your own router; the screens under it stay presentational.
